viral_threads.title: 3 Psychological Traps That Destroy 90% of Blitz Players
tweets:
1/5 You don't lose blitz games because your opponent calculated further than you.

You lose because your nervous system hijacked your decision-making under 15 seconds.

Here are 3 psychological traps that destroy 90% of speed chess players (and how to fix them): 🧵

2/5 Trap 1: The Premove Panic.

When the clock drops below 5 seconds, players premove hope checks instead of solid defensive moves.

Rule: Never premove when your king has no luft. One discovered check ends the game instantly.

3/5 Trap 2: Playing the Material, Not the Clock.

Being up a rook in blitz is meaningless if you have 3 seconds and your opponent has 20.

Simplify the position. Every capture and trade bleeds clock. When ahead on time, create complications; when ahead on material, trade pieces immediately.

4/5 Trap 3: Ghost Threats.

Amateur players spend 10 precious seconds reacting to moves that do not threaten anything.

Ask one question: 'What is their check, capture, or threat?' If none exists, advance your own plan without flinching.

5/5 Master these habits by reviewing your games move by move in our free Academy.
